policy: Entries are conservative migration signals for scripts and skills. Status values describe the rollout signal, not a guarantee that every legacy file has already been removed from every install.

entries.title: Meeting intelligence and Granola legacy path
entries.impact: Local installs may still contain Granola-specific automation, config keys, logs, or references. Treat them as optional legacy integration state, not a required production default.
entries.migration_guidance: If a vault depends on Granola sync, preserve local automation intentionally. Otherwise prefer the standard /process-meetings workflow and remove local Granola credentials, launch agents, and generated logs after confirming no active dependency.

detection.replacement: /process-meetings with production-safe meeting notes and person/task updates

entries.title: Demo mode legacy surfaces
entries.impact: Demo fixtures and demo-mode commands are sample-only surfaces. They should not be migrated into personal production vault content unless a user explicitly wants sample data.
entries.migration_guidance: Keep production data separate from demo fixtures. During updates, preserve user-created content and treat demo-mode files as replaceable product samples.

detection.replacement: production templates and docs without personal sample data

entries.title: Screenpipe setup legacy surfaces
entries.impact: Screenpipe setup appears as a beta or optional integration signal and should not be assumed present in production installs.
entries.migration_guidance: Do not auto-enable Screenpipe during updates. If local notes reference Screenpipe, leave them in place and require an explicit user opt-in before configuring any capture workflow.

detection.replacement: no default replacement; explicit opt-in only

entries.title: AI setup and status legacy skills
entries.impact: Older setup/status skills may overlap with current setup, health-check, and update-preflight flows.
entries.migration_guidance: Prefer /setup for onboarding, /health-check for diagnostics, and /amp-update-preflight for update readiness. Keep local custom skill aliases only if they are intentionally maintained.

entries.title: Slack intel skill rename
entries.impact: Local installs may reference the older slack-intel-custom name while production guidance may use slack-intel.
entries.migration_guidance: Prefer slack-intel as the stable command name when available. Preserve slack-intel-custom only as a local custom override or compatibility alias.
